body.question: Xi Jinping out before 2027?
body.description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if China's General Secretary of the Communist Party, Xi Jinping, is removed from power for any length of time between July 3, 2025, and December 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

CCP General Secretary Xi Jinping will be considered removed from power if he announces his resignation from his role as General Secretary, or is otherwise dismissed, detained, disqualified, or otherwise loses his position or is prevented from fulfilling his duties as General Secretary within this market's timeframe.

The primary resolution source for this market will be a consensus of credible reporting.

eventMetadata.context_description: Xi Jinping's consolidated control over the Chinese Communist Party, military, and state institutions continues to underpin trader consensus that he will remain in power through the end of 2026. With the next National Congress not scheduled until 2027 and no public signs of elite-level challenges or health-related incapacity emerging in recent months, the short resolution window reinforces the high probability assigned to his continued tenure. Historical patterns of leadership stability since the 2018 constitutional changes and the absence of scheduled succession mechanisms further align with current market pricing. Low-probability shifts could still arise from sudden health events, unanticipated domestic crises, or internal factional realignments, though verifiable indicators of such developments remain absent.

body.question: Will Gavin Newsom win the 2028 Democratic presidential nomination?
body.description:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if the named individual wins and accepts the 2028 nomination of the Democratic Party for U.S. president. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

The resolution source for this market will be a consensus of official Democratic Party sources.

Any replacement of the democratic nominee before election day will not change the resolution of the market.

eventMetadata.context_description: The fragmented Democratic field for 2028 keeps trader consensus tightly clustered among leading options, with Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, Gavin Newsom, and Jon Ossoff priced within a few points amid no formal announcements or major endorsements as of mid-2026. AOC draws strength from progressive voter coalitions and early-state polling edges, while Newsom leverages executive experience and broader name recognition, and Ossoff benefits from Senate profile and fundraising momentum. Recent DNC primary calendar shifts toward South Carolina and New Hampshire have spotlighted regional advantages without yet consolidating support. Ideological debates over centrist versus progressive paths, combined with lingering questions around 2024 performance, sustain uncertainty and prevent any single contender from pulling ahead decisively.
